title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 217: The Vanishing Vault: Light Pollution
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 217 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Vanishing Vault: Light Pollution and the Architecture of Darkness

Paragraph 1. For thousands of years, people watched the night sky carefully. Farmers looked at the stars to decide when to plant seeds, and sailors used stars to cross wide oceans. Over the past one hundred years, however, bright electric city lights changed our nights. Today, more than eighty percent of people in the world live under bright, polluted night skies. In big cities across the United States and Europe, yellow light fills the sky every evening.

Paragraph 2. This bright night haze happens because street lights shine up into the sky instead of pointing down at the ground. The upward light hits tiny drops of water and dust in the air and bounces back down. Because of this bright glow, city people cannot see the Milky Way or small stars anymore. Often, only the moon and a few very bright planets remain visible above cities.

Paragraph 3. Too much night light also hurts wild animals and human health. Flying insects get confused by bright street lamps and fly in circles until they get tired or eaten by bats. Baby sea turtles hatch on beaches and look for bright moonlight on the sea, so bright hotel lights pull them away from water toward dangerous roads. In humans, blue light from street lamps and phone screens hurts healthy sleep and can raise the risk of heart problems.

Paragraph 4. Luckily, cities do not need to turn off all lights to fix this problem. Engineers suggest placing covers on street lamps so light shines only downward. Cities are also replacing harsh blue-white bulbs with soft warm yellow lights. In northern Chile, new lighting laws keep the night sky dark for space scientists while cutting city electricity costs by over thirty percent.
